question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=1 - \frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$. Rewrite with powers, then differentiate term by term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=(-1x^{- \frac{1}{2}})+(-1x^{-1})+(1)\\
f'(x)&=\frac{1}{x^{2}} + \frac{1}{2 x^{\frac{3}{2}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(4\right)=\frac{1}{\left(4\right)^{2}} + \frac{1}{2 \left(4\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}=\frac{1}{8}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)}=-8.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)&=-8\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)\\
y&=- 8 x+\left(32\right)+\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\\
y&=\frac{129}{4} - 8 x
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=-8$ and $b=\frac{129}{4}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=(1x^{\frac{1}{3}})+(1x^{1})+(1)\\
f'(x)&=1 + \frac{1}{3 x^{\frac{2}{3}}}
\end{aligned}

$$
m_t=f'\left(1\right)=1 + \frac{1}{3 \left(1\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}=\frac{4}{3}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)}=- \frac{3}{4}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=(2x^{\frac{1}{3}})+(-1x^{1})+(1)\\
f'(x)&=-1 + \frac{2}{3 x^{\frac{2}{3}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
m_t=f'\left(1\right)=-1 + \frac{2}{3 \left(1\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}=- \frac{1}{3}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(- \frac{1}{3}\right)}=3.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(2\right)&=3\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)\\

\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=3$ and $b=-1$.

$$

$$
